name: Blancpain Carrousel Répétition Minutes
description: This grand complication is the premiere in the history of watchmaking, combining a one-minute flying carrousel and a minute repeater with cathedral chimes. One-minute flying carrousel Designed to counteract the perturbations induced by gravity on the accuracy of watches, the carrousel is a rare and fascinating complication. Blancpain has revived this device and incorporated it into a wristwatch for the first time.

name: Hublot Big Bang Unico Golf
description: Pioneering Watch Movements The Art of Fusion is expressed right through to the heart of the movement. Simple watches with innovative watchmaking concepts, Hublot has created a range of unique “in-house” movements. A unique design of the Unico automatic chronograph. An unparalleled power reserve of Meca-10, Tourbillon and MP-11 calibers. A revolutionary motor approach with 11 MP-05 barrels and 50-day power reserve. In its “Art of Fusion,” Hublot carries out a perfect symbiosis between functionality, architecture and design

name: Jaeger LeCoultre Master Ultra Thin Tourbillon
description: 40 mm - Pink Gold 750/1000 (18 carats) - Automatic winding. In an aperture at 6 o'clock, the Master Ultra Thin Tourbillon watch gives way to the spellbinding ballet of its tourbillon, enhanced by a row of diamonds that adorns and encircle its bezel. Designed to enhance the spectacle of the tourbillon and its new gold bridge, the setting of its 68 diamonds exemplify the talent of the master craftsmen who meticulously select each gemstone before working to bring out its shine and brilliance. Visible under its sapphire crystal, the case-back of the watch offers another, equally fascinating, spectacle: That of its mechanical self-winding movement, the Jaeger-LeCoultre Caliber 978G.

name: F.P. Journe Tourbillon Souverain à Remontoire d'Égalité
description: The F.P. Journe Tourbillon Souverain à Remontoire d’Egalité is known for its pioneering mechanical innovations, including a constant force device (remontoir d’égalité) designed for enhanced timekeeping accuracy. This mechanism ensures that energy from the mainspring is consistently delivered to the escapement, reducing variations in timekeeping as the watch unwinds. Additionally, the watch features a "dead seconds" complication (seconde morte), where the seconds hand remains stationary until each second has passed, an uncommon feature that provides precise time indication and highlights F.P. Journe's commitment to horological precision.
